protocol: All three scenarios start with the same drone state, measurement-noise settings and random draws, pretrained neural policy, MPPI settings, and zero initial learned correction. All enable dynamics learning and policy adaptation during flight, with no preliminary data collection. Gatekeeper admits controller updates only with an accepted candidate. The changed settings are the hidden drag/bias and whether Gatekeeper is enabled. Each scenario is allowed up to 30 seconds and ends early if a gate is missed or the course clearance is violated. This is a selected example, not a collision-rate estimate or an unconditional safety guarantee. A lap is eight ordered gates. Clearance is the remaining distance to a course boundary after accounting for the drone's size. A reported gate collision is separately confirmed by overlap between the recorded drone sphere and a gate-frame bar.

outcome.label: Contact with Gate 6
outcome.basis: Recorded drone sphere intersects a gate-frame bar

search.description: We searched for an illustrative failure by varying the course geometry, the MPCC progress and centerline-error weights, the speed used to initialize MPPI, and the simulated drone's hidden drag and constant acceleration bias. The settings below all remain inside the original assumed force limits: drag at most 0.035 m⁻¹ and bias magnitude at most 0.2 m/s². Directional drag opposes motion along a fixed axis; it never adds kinetic energy and obeys the same norm bound. The neural controller settings, learning procedure, command limits and Gatekeeper checks were not retuned. All completed trials without Gatekeeper and with unknown forces are listed. The final three scenarios share exactly the same course, planner weights and initial conditions. The selected forces are used unchanged with Gatekeeper. This deliberately selected example shows a failure mechanism; it does not estimate how often collisions occur.

outcome.basis: Negative recorded clearance; physical gate contact is not established
